title: I told Opus "make graphics that only flagship phones can run". this is what it made for my asteroids style browser game
author: FotoRe_store
selftext:
all of it is procedural, no image files, runs in the phone browser on webgl. the background is ink drifting in fog, slowly going from cold to warm colors, and the light moves around the screen once a minute. rocks are black obsidian with cracks glued with gold, like kintsugi. there are no explosions, a hit rock gets annihilated and that stirs up the ink flows right where it was. Opus named it "obsidian in ink and fog"

my iphone 16 runs it smooth, my old mi 9 basically dies lol. oh and the ship is controlled by your palm in the air, the phone uses its speaker and mic as a sonar

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body: Can't tell if this post is sarcasm but... Yeah those are terrible graphics for what a phone can run.  Having one phone lag and your other phone run it well is not any kind of metric.. it just means its wasting processing power.

replies.author: FotoRe_store
replies.body:
not sarcasm lol. its more a benchmark than a skin. the task was to take the simplest scene there is, a ship and some rocks, and see how far a phone gpu can go in a browser, so "wasting processing power" is literally the brief. before this we tried a bunch of backgrounds, black hole, rain, underwater, particles and others, most of them were either pretty or readable, not both

how the ink works: its not a texture or a video, its math for every pixel every frame. the base is 3d noise where the third dimension is time, so it keeps flowing. then that noise is warped by noise, and that again by noise (domain warping), thats where the smoke like swirls come from. one ink pixel is 5 noise calls with 5 octaves each, plus a few more for the thin veins along the ridges and a cheap copy for the lighting, so around 40 3d noise lookups per pixel. and the game is inside the same calculation, the ship wake, the rock wakes and every hit shift where the ink is read from, so nothing can be baked in advance

the fog is a second ink layer behind, bigger, darker, fewer octaves, half resolution. where the near ink is thin you see the far one through it, thats the depth. then theres a light outside the screen that goes around once a minute. it doesnt light things directly, it makes rims on the ink edges facing it and shafts of light through the gaps, for that every pixel takes 12 samples on the way to the light to see how much ink is in the way. the palette goes from cold to warm and back over the same minute. all of it is in 16 bit float linear light and tone mapped at the end

why its hard for a phone: iphone 16 screen is about 3 million pixels, at full res that would be over 100 million noise lookups per frame. so the near ink updates the top and bottom half on alternating frames, the far ink is half res, the wallpaper is 1.5 px per css px instead of 3, only the objects are full res. even then its still over 20 million noise lookups per frame, 60 times a second. phones also heat up and throttle after a few minutes, so if fps stays under \~50 for 2 seconds it steps down by itself. and the same phone is running the sonar at the same time, so the gpu cant be pushed to 100%.
